facts.statement: The researchers used a cross-sectional study design to examine 562 people who were receiving peritoneal dialysis.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Sleep quality was measured using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, while sleep duration was recorded in hours per night.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Sarcopenia was identified using the 2025 Asian Working Group criteria.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Sleep duration had a U-shaped relationship with sarcopenia, where the risk was lowest at about 7.29 hours of sleep per night.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Poorer sleep quality, indicated by a higher PSQI score, was linked to a higher likelihood of sarcopenia.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Poor sleep quality and short sleep duration were linked to sarcopenia partly through their connection to higher body fat percentage, but long sleep duration showed no such indirect link.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: While albumin levels interacted with body fat in the analysis, this interaction did not significantly change the indirect pathway linking sleep to sarcopenia.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors state that because the study was cross-sectional, the results suggest associations but cannot prove that sleep problems cause sarcopenia.
facts.subject: humans
